title: n8n keeps no ordered business record because execution data is prunable and pruning is on by default
content:
n8n keeps no ordered business record. Its execution data is prunable, and pruning is on by default — so the history of what the automation did is a retention-managed cache, not a log. Nothing has to be misconfigured for the record to vanish; the default configuration is the failure mode.

The resulting position is straightforward: Powerhouse is the durable log the automation writes to as it runs. The workflow keeps doing what it does well — triggering, branching, calling APIs — and each business-relevant branch also emits an attributed, append-only entry that outlives the execution row. There is no contest over ownership of the automation layer.

This is the cleanest instance in the corpus of the general finding that open-source business tools do not keep an immutable attributed log by default. Most tools in the survey leave a mutable record; n8n's default actively deletes one. For the seven German integrators carrying this finding, that makes the gap demonstrable in the client's own installation rather than argued from documentation.
